newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO say they agree on Hebron observers.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO say they agree on Hebron observers.

text.p: Israel and the Palestinians said on Monday they had reached agreement to send more international observers into the West Bank town of Hebron.

U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross meanwhile shuttled between Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat trying to forge a broader accord extending self-rule to the volatile town.

Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said he and Israeli officials, meeting in Jericho, had concluded an agreement to increase the number of observers in Hebron to 210 from 30 once the self-rule deal is done.
Erekat said the signing would be in a day or two.
"We reached agreement basically on all the points and now the agreements go to those in charge on each side. It's hard to estimate when it will be signed," an Israeli foreign ministry spokesman said.
Under the agreement 180 peacekeepers from Denmark, Italy, Norway, Sweden, Switzerland and Turkey would join 30 Norwegian observers already stationed in the town.

The new peacekeepers would arrive only after Israel and the PLO conclude an overall deal to extend self-rule to Hebron, burial place of the biblical Abraham and home to 100,000 Palestinians and 400 Jewish settlers.
Security issues and other concerns over the last 10 months have delayed the Israeli handover to Arafat's PLO.

"We have made a lot of progress. There is not a lot that separates the parties but there is not an agreement yet and we don't have an agreement until everything is resolved. And everything is not resolved," Ross said after meeting Netanyahu.
Ross was due to meet Arafat later in self-ruled Bethlehem.

But a Palestinian official accused him of bias. Israel's newspaper Haaretz had quoted Ross and other U.S. officials as saying Netanyahu, stretched "to the outer limits of his flexibility," could concede no more.

"I am astonished by Dennis Ross's statements which expressed his completely biased disposition," Arafat's aide Marwan Kanafani told Israel Radio's Arabic service. "I think these statements harm the peace process."
